# About NFTCDN
* Established in 2022
* Testnet (Preview & Pre-Prod) and Mainnet coverage of all native assets
* Service(s) offered on pay-per-API-use tiered pricing model
* Existing customers include Verspr, Eternl, Tokeo, NEWM, NMKR, Pool.pm
* Have served 800+ million API requests as of April-2025
* Currently running with 100% uptime since launch

# How is NFTCDN different from a basic CDN (e.g. Cloudflare, Vercel, etc)
- **NFTCDN is purpose-built for Cardano**: NFTCDN is more than a CDN. Direct API access to `/metadata`, `/image`, `/file` native assets using only their fingerprint ID. Cloudflare offers no blockchain/NFT support; this would have to be custom built by devs.
- **Multi-protocol/system support**: NFTCDN auto-handles multimedia storage fetching from IPFS, Arweave, HTTP, on-chain. Cloudflare requires devs to build fetch/parsing logic manually on their own infra setup.
- **Standards-aware infra**: NFTCDN supports CIP-25, 68, v0.01 and adapts as they evolve. Cloudflare has no protocol awareness - devs must implement parsing module compliance manually and cater for human error and edge cases.
- **No infra required**: NFTCDN handles full resolution flow (parsing, error fall-back, and format support) out of the box. Cloudflare needs origin setup and content pre-hosted on their proprietary solutions.
- **Real-time chain indexing**: Native assets state updated live (minting & updating) from chain. Cloudflare requires manual indexing, pointer mgmt, and cache invalidation.
- **Cloudflare TOS risk**: Large or non-web file caching (image, audio, video, 3D files) is restricted; in-production use will violate TOS unless using proprietary paid products (Stream/Images/R2, c. ~$5k+/yr).    
- **Global cross-app caching**: NFTCDN caches assets at the asset level, so cache `HITS` benefit all products (websites & dApps). Cloudflare caches per domain/site - no sharing resulting in low CDN performance resulting in higher cache `MISS` states.
- **Built-in content safety**: NFTCDN provides CSP headers + dev. controls over rendering. Cloudflare lacks native asset-specific safeguards, increasing risk of suspension due to embedded malicious multimedia content.

* In the event of non-renewal, NFTCDN will revert to a paid subscription model
* To mitigate risk of delays in the 2026 Cardano budget process, a 18 (+1) month SLA has been proposed

attributes.problem_statement:
# Background - Native Assets
- Native assets (NFTs & FTs) are widely used on Cardano across diverse use cases
- Often used to store multimedia content - images, music, videos, documents, etc
- Media is stored on decentralised systems - IPFS, Arweave, and on-chain embeds
- Centralised storage options also used - HTTP, FTP & commercial cloud providers
- File locations are referenced as links within the native asset’s metadata

# Pain Point - Technical Complexity
- Accessing native asset media requires querying the blockchain (Cardano node + DB-Sync)
- And fetching content via middleware (e.g. IPFS gateway/node)
- Apps must handle this process programmatically, at scale, with robust exception handling
- Developers face challenges from:
    - Human error (e.g. typos in metadata links)
    - Evolving standards (e.g. NFT v0.01, CIP-25, CIP-68)
    - Protocol updates (e.g. Chang HF impacting Node & DB-Sync)
- Performance, efficiency, and reliability must be maintained across all layers
- Apps must build and maintain complex, resilient backend infrastructure to support native asset display as both a capability & feature

# Solution – NFTCDN
- NFTCDN is a managed Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) provider
- Provides high-availability native asset media & metadata delivery via globally distributed, high-speed Content Delivery Network
- Developers access content using only the native asset fingerprint ID - no complex setup needed
- Eliminates the need to design, build, test, & maintain complex end-to-end infra
- Enables focus on innovation of their product - not backend ops

# Problem Statement - Cost to Build/Access
- Building native asset delivery infra in-house costs ~$100,000 and 9+ months (internal benchmarks)
- NFTCDN solves upfront CAPEX/OPEX needs
- But we are a paid service (pay-per-API-call) - limiting adoption
- Only well-funded teams have been able to integrate NFTCDN to date
- Many projects cannot afford the cost, leading to delays, increased risk, or total shutdown
- Market headwinds further impacted adoption, with some customers forced to shut down due to reduced user base

# Proposal – The Ask
- Fund NFTCDN to make it free for all Cardano builders for 18 months under an SLA contract
- Cover operational & infra scale-up costs to deliver enterprise-grade Native Asset CDN
- Enables us to provide our solution to the Cardano community for free
- Removes cost barriers, fuelling innovation, faster development, and wider adoption

* Eliminate up-front infrastructure costs (~$100,000 per product) for native asset display
* Accelerate product development by 9+ months by removing the need to build and maintain complex, scalable infrastructure
* Immediate cost avoidance opportunity of **~$1.5m** and **~23,400 developer hours** across 15+ existing NFTCDN customers
* Additional cost avoidance opportunity of **~$1m** and **~15,600 developer hours** during proposal funding cycle by onboarding at least 10 additional products
* Maintenance & operational cost avoidance of **$3m** for 25 NFTCDN users during proposal funding cycle
* Proposal cost of ~$320k with a **ROI of 17.20x**

# ROI Calculations Breakdown

- **Typical development cost of infrastructure to support native asset display:**
  - ~9 months / 1,560 dev hours
  - ~$100k (developer, PM, infra) per product

- **Typical annual running & maintenance cost:**
  - ~$100,000 in salaries for labour (back- & front-end, networking, storage, cyber security, admin)
  - ~$20,000 infra cost (servers, hosting, licenses)

- **Tasks avoided by using NFTCDN:**
  - Cardano node + DB-Sync + Other Cardano software setup & upgrades
  - Middleware for native Asset metadata parsing (CIP-25, CIP-68, v0.01)
  - Middleware for metadata error and edge case handling
  - Integration with IPFS, Arweave, HTTP, on-chain storage systems/protocols
  - Middleware for multimedia content optimisation
  - Security handling (e.g., malware in native assets)
  - Real-time monitoring pipeline of native asset minting & updates
  - End-to-end routing pipeline, including maintenance and updating
  - Regulatory compliance review & management process overhead
  - Performance, reliability, and redundancy infrastructure

- **Savings for Current NFTCDN Users (15 active projects)**
  - Dev Hours Savings = 23,400 (1,560 hrs x 15 current projects)
  - Labour & Infra Savings = $1.5M in cost avoidance ($100k x 15 current projects)

- **Savings from +10 new projects onboarded during proposal period (conservative est.)**
  - Adds 15,600 dev. hours and $1M in additional savings for newly onboarded projects into NFTCDN for duration of proposal (18 months)

- **Savings for on-going maint. & ops cost (25 projects)**
  - Adds $3m in additional savings ($100k + $20k x 25 total projects using NFTCDN)

- **Total value returned:**
  - ~39,000 dev hours saved for initial development
  - ~$5.5M total ecosystem cost avoidance

- **Proposal cost:** ~$320k
  - **Estimated ROI:** ~17.2x
  - Equivalent of ~19 years of cumulative dev time saved

# Intangible Benefits

* **Removes Adoption Barriers** - Eliminates financial (OPEX/CAPEX) & technical (dev. complexity) barriers to entry
* **Accelerates Time-to-Market** - Enables fast and easy integration of native asset features/capabilities
* **Frees Up Product Teams** - Reduces backend overhead, letting teams focus on core feature dev, growth & adoption
* **Boosts Developer Adoption** - Makes accessible for early-stage, under/unfunded and community (free-product) builders
* **Enables Broader Innovation** - Enables exploration of new native asset use cases (RWA, identity, media, education)
* **Future-Proof Native Asset Delivery** - Adapts to evolving standards; all users benefit from shared upgrades and fixes
* **Eliminates Redundancy** - Shared infrastructure avoids every project building redundant, costly systems
* **Improves End-User Experience** - A high-speed, enterprise-grade, globally distributed CDN for multimedia content substantially improves loading speeds
* **Drives Ecosystem Growth** – Native asset adoption across more apps creates compounding utility and user adoption
* **Aligns with Cardano's Goals & Roadmap** – Directly supports Cardano's 2025 roadmaps goals around simplifying developer experience, increasing real-world utility and improving end-user experience

- Centralised storage options also used - HTTP, FTP & commercial cloud providers
- File locations are referenced as links within the native asset’s metadata

# Pain Point - Technical Complexity
- Accessing native asset media requires querying the blockchain (Cardano node + DB-Sync)
- And fetching content via middleware (e.g. IPFS gateway/node)
- Apps must handle this process programmatically, at scale, with robust exception handling
- Developers face challenges from:
    - Human error (e.g. typos in metadata links)
    - Evolving standards (e.g. NFT v0.01, CIP-25, CIP-68)
    - Protocol updates (e.g. Chang HF impacting Node & DB-Sync)
- Performance, efficiency, and reliability must be maintained across all layers
- Apps must build and maintain complex, resilient backend infrastructure to support native asset display as both a capability & feature

# Solution – NFTCDN
- NFTCDN is a managed Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) provider
- Provides high-availability native asset media & metadata delivery via globally distributed, high-speed Content Delivery Network
- Developers access content using only the native asset fingerprint ID - no complex setup needed
- Eliminates the need to design, build, test, & maintain complex end-to-end infra
- Enables focus on innovation of their product - not backend ops

# Problem Statement - Cost to Build/Access

- NFTCDN solves upfront CAPEX/OPEX needs

- Cover operational & infra scale-up costs to deliver enterprise-grade Native Asset CDN

- Removes cost barriers, fuelling innovation, faster development, and wider adoption

attributes.problem_statement:
# Background - Native Assets
- Native assets (NFTs & FTs) are widely used on Cardano across diverse use cases
- Often used to store multimedia content - images, music, videos, documents, etc
- Media is stored on decentralised systems - IPFS, Arweave, and on-chain embeds
- Centralised storage options also used - HTTP, FTP & commercial cloud providers
- File locations are referenced as links within the native asset’s metadata

# Pain Point - Technical Complexity
- Accessing native asset media requires querying the blockchain (Cardano node + DB-Sync)
- And fetching content via middleware (e.g. IPFS gateway/node)
- Apps must handle this process programmatically, at scale, with robust exception handling
- Developers face challenges from:
    - Human error (e.g. typos in metadata links)
    - Evolving standards (e.g. NFT v0.01, CIP-25, CIP-68)
    - Protocol updates (e.g. Chang HF impacting Node & DB-Sync)
- Performance, efficiency, and reliability must be maintained across all layers
- Apps must build and maintain complex, resilient backend infrastructure to support native asset display as both a capability & feature

# Solution – NFTCDN
- NFTCDN is a managed Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) provider
- Provides high-availability native asset media & metadata delivery via globally distributed, high-speed Content Delivery Network
- Developers access content using only the native asset fingerprint ID - no complex setup needed
- Eliminates the need to design, build, test, & maintain complex end-to-end infra
- Enables focus on innovation of their product - not backend ops

# Problem Statement - Cost to Build/Access
- Building native asset delivery infra in-house costs ~$100,000 and 9+ months (internal benchmarks)
- NFTCDN solves upfront CAPEX/OPEX needs
- But we are a paid service (pay-per-API-call) - limiting adoption
- Only well-funded teams have been able to integrate NFTCDN to date
- Many projects cannot afford the cost, leading to delays, increased risk, or total shutdown
- Market headwinds further impacted adoption, with some customers forced to shut down due to reduced user base

# Proposal – The Ask
- Fund NFTCDN to make it free for all Cardano builders
- Cover operational & infra scale-up costs to deliver enterprise-grade Native Asset CDN
- Enables us to provide our solution to the Cardano community for free
- Removes cost barriers, fuelling innovation, faster development, and wider adoption

attributes.problem_statement:
# Background - Native Assets
- Native assets (NFTs & FTs) are widely used on Cardano across diverse use cases
- Often used to store multimedia content - images, music, videos, documents, etc
- Media is stored on decentralised systems - IPFS, Arweave, and on-chain embeds
- Centralised storage options also used - HTTP, FTP & commercial cloud providers
- File locations are referenced as links within the native asset’s metadata

# Pain Point - Technical Complexity
- Accessing native asset media requires querying the blockchain (Cardano node + DB-Sync)
- And fetching content via middleware (e.g. IPFS gateway/node)
- Apps must handle this process programmatically, at scale, with robust exception handling
- Developers face challenges from:
    - Human error (e.g. typos in metadata links)
    - Evolving standards (e.g. NFT v0.01, CIP-25, CIP-68)
    - Protocol updates (e.g. Chang HF impacting Node & DB-Sync)
- Performance, efficiency, and reliability must be maintained across all layers
- Apps must build and maintain complex, resilient backend infrastructure to support native asset display as both a capability & feature

# Solution – NFTCDN
- NFTCDN is a managed Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) provider
- Provides high-availability native asset media & metadata delivery via globally distributed, high-speed Content Delivery Network
- Developers access content using only the native asset fingerprint ID - no complex setup needed
- Eliminates the need to design, build, test, & maintain complex end-to-end infra
- Enables focus on innovation of their product - not backend ops

# Problem Statement - Cost to Build/Access
- Building native asset delivery infra in-house costs ~$100,000 and 9+ months (internal benchmarks)
- NFTCDN solves upfront CAPEX/OPEX needs
- But we are a paid service (pay-per-API-call) - limiting adoption
- Only well-funded teams have been able to integrate NFTCDN to date
- Many projects cannot afford the cost, leading to delays, increased risk, or total shutdown
- Market headwinds further impacted adoption, with some customers forced to shut down due to reduced user base

# Proposal – The Ask
- Fund NFTCDN to make it free for all Cardano builders
- Cover operational & infra scale-up costs to deliver enterprise-grade Native Asset CDN
- Enables us to provide our solution to the Cardano community for free
- Removes cost barriers, fuelling innovation, faster development, and wider adoption

# Background - Native Assets


Native Assets (non-fungible tokens and fungible tokens) are widely used on Cardano across various use cases, including as a medium to store multimedia content such as pictures, songs, movies, documents and more. These multimedia files are stored predominantly on decentralised storage protocols and systems such as IPFS, Arweave, on-chain embeds, and also centralised ones such as HTTP, FTP and commercial cloud providers and are referenced as links within the native asset's metadata. 


# Pain point - Complexity


Once a native asset is minted on the blockchain, an individual can view the reference links to these files by querying the blockchain (e.g. using Cardano DB-Sync) and access them thereafter through middleware (e.g. IPFS gateway/node). For apps, this task must be handled programmatically, at scale, and with extensive exception handling. Developers must account for factors such as human error (e.g. typographical errors in reference links within the native asset metadata), evolving native asset standards (e.g. NFT v0.01, CIP-25, CIP-68) and Cardano protocol updates (e.g. Chang HF impacting Cardano node & DB-Sync) - notwithstanding performance, efficiency and reliability considerations at both the product and end-user level. Any app building on Cardano that seeks to integrate native assets display on their product as both a backend capability and a user-facing feature must therefore build and continually work to maintain a robust, performant, reliable and resilient end-to-end infrastructure.


# Solution - NFTCDN 


NFTCDN is a managed Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) platform providing high-availability multimedia and metadata delivery for Cardano native assets via simple APIs. Our API endpoints streamline the display of NFT multimedia content and metadata through its globally distributed, high-speed Content Delivery Network (CDN). Using only the native asset fingerprint ID within our endpoints, developers can easily access the multimedia and metadata content. In doing so, we eliminate the need to design, build, test and maintain a complex end-to-end infrastructure to do so, thereby enabling projects to enhance their NFT-related product offerings, accelerate time-to-market, and focus on innovation of their own product rather than infrastructure management.

attributes.comment_text:
Given that NFTCDN is already operating as a for-profit service, is it fair and appropriate to use Cardano Treasury funds to fully subsidize the service for all developers? 
This might add a bit of complexity, but if the goal is to make native assets accessible to more developers and projects, might that be achieved more effectively by being more targeted, such as only subsidizing the costs with a discounted 6-month free trial for new projects?

Hi Yuta, honoured to have your feedback. Addressing each point below:


> **“Given that NFTCDN is already operating as a for-profit service...”** 
* Yes - NFTCDN is a live Infrastructure-as-a-Service product w/ proven & credible reliability, performance & quality since launch (2022). That’s exactly why this proposal is low-risk & high-impact.


> **“Is it fair to use Cardano Treasury funds...?”** 
* We believe it is. No other service in industry offers this functionality today. Treasury funding isn’t subsidising a business - it’s enabling **community-wide access** to essential infrastructure. Once free-model is activated, paid-model will be disabled. Proposal costs have been highly compressed to prioritise accessibility, not profit margin.


> **“Is it appropriate to use Cardano Treasury funds?”** 
* Yes, absolutely; this is a strategic infrastructure investment for Cardano aligned with the 2025 Goals & Roadmap. Native asset media delivery isn’t optional, but fundamental, for wallets, marketplaces, & multimedia dApp products. The proposal eliminates technical & financial barriers, accelerates product development, enables innovation; drawing more users & utilisation - benefits far exceeding proposal cost. Also, Catalyst isn’t suitable for this (not net-new innovation); Treasury is the appropriate route.


> **“...to fully subsidise the service for all developers?”** 
* Full subsidy ensures **equitable access**. It supports:
 * Existing paying projects 
 * Early-stage teams not yet generating revenue 
 * Community / open source tools like Pool.pm that provide immense value but don’t monetise


> **“Might a targeted model (e.g. 6-month trial) be more effective?”** 
* As you say, a targeted model introduces complexity (eligibility, vetting, verification, governance) & also uncertainty. Projects need long-term cost predictability to confidently build. A trial / partial subsidy would exclude many who need it most & raise the admin/ops burden, resulting in higher proposal cost.
* This proposal is actually **simpler, cheaper, && more inclusive** - benefiting the entire ecosystem without being partial or adding delays.


Our intent is not to extract funds from the Cardano Treasury, but to **deliver value into the Cardano ecosystem** by offering a vital infrastructure service, not unlike Intersect, for a fundamental blockchain capability - native assets display - which cannot be implemented w/o significant up-front investments.


Trust this addresses your points.

Hi Yuta, thank you once again for your feedback. Responding below point by point.

> "1. Does the benefit of this proposal disproportionately favor NFT and RWA projects? How will general dApp developers and end users also gain value from this investment?"

NFTCDN’s service - and this proposal - is agnostic of native asset type. Whether a project uses fungible tokens (FTs) or non-fungible tokens (NFTs), NFTCDN allows them to retrieve and display a native asset’s metadata and multimedia (images, audio, video, documents, 3D models, HTML, etc.) via a simple API call.

*** Value to the Ecosystem -- We want to make NFTCDN free to support:
1. Existing products that rely on native assets
2. New use cases beyond just NFT art or RWAs, removing cost and complexity barriers

These use cases span across industries such as:
- Gaming (in-game assets, avatars, loot drops)
- Media (ownership, royalties, exclusive content)
- Publishing (tokenized books, archives)
- Ticketing (concerts, memberships, access passes)
- Retail (supply chain authenticity, warranties)
- Legal (tokenized contracts / deeds)
- Identity (DIDs, licenses, voting tokens)
- Finance (fractionalized assets, yield-bearing tokens)
- Healthcare (medical records, selective data sharing)

** Value to Developers -- Developers save months of time and significant cost. Instead of building complex infrastructure to support native asset display, they can integrate NFTCDN in minutes using virtually one line of code; allowing them to focus on their product, not backend operations.

*** Value to End-Users -- Users benefit from:
- Performance -- Sub-millisecond load times; via our global CDN (faster, smoother UX)
- Reliability -- 100% uptime; no broken images or missing multimedia content
- Comprehensive Solution -- Support for all major NFT/FT standards, all major native asset multimedia types and storage systems/protocols

> "2. What is the basis for the claimed savings of ~23,400 development hours and $1.5M in cost avoidance for existing customers? Can the estimation methodology be disclosed?"

No problem. Some context first:

Building native asset infrastructure from scratch is complex and time-consuming. A product that wants to display native assets needs to, at a high-level:
• Set up a Cardano node, DB-Sync, and monitoring tools
• Handle evolving CIP standards (currently 4 for NFTs, 2 for FTs)
• Integrate with multiple multimedia storage systems/protocols (IPFS, Arweave, HTTP, on-chain)
• Build middleware to manage invalid metadata and edge cases
• Address security concerns behind native assets as anyone can upload anything, incl. malware which can get your product blocked by ISPs around the world
• Account for performance, reliability and failover infrastructure

This is where NFTCDN comes in. You sign-up, implement our API endpoint, virtually 1 line of code - and you're set. 
So you don't have to do all of the things mentioned above, avoiding the cost and development time involved.

• It took us ~9 months of dev time (40 hours per week, 9 months, i.e. 1,560 hours) to design, build, test and deploy the aforementioned end-to-end infrastructure.
• 1x Developer, 1x Project Manager and infrastructure investments were a total of c. $120k (we've rounded it down to $100k for ease of calculations). 
• Additionally, we're not counting maintenance/running costs over the lifetime of the product (~$10k per month).

- We currently have 15 customers actively using NFTCDN (Eternl, VESPR, Tokeo, NEWM, etc).
